Python: terrain correction

Source: vignettes/articles/python-terrain-correction.Rmd
python-terrain-correction.Rmd

Altitude and slope combined with an elevation model read at the plots: the terrain sources and the descriptors read from them, the coded and neural terrain fields, and the correction itself. Correcting altitude and slope with an elevation model walks through a fit; a model suite corrects its targets through SuitePredictor.predict(terrain=...).

All of the Python reference

Installation 

# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("gcol33/resolve/r")

# The engine library, downloaded once
library(resolveR)
resolve.install_backend()
pip install resolve-core

Terrain sources 

TerrainGrids(dir, cache_tiles=16)
open_terrain_field(path, device="cpu")
TerrainCodedField(path, cache_blocks=4096)
TerrainField(path, device="cpu", cache_tiles=64)

A TerrainSource answers the elevation at any coordinate. TerrainGrids reads elevation grids on disk: a tiles.json listing float32 .npy tiles, each with its shape, the position of its first cell centre and its cell spacing (pixel is point, rows from north to south). open_terrain_field opens a terrain field file of either format from its header: a TerrainCodedField, coded with a bounded error per cell, or a TerrainField, one neural field per tile. Every source has elevation(lat, lon) (bilinear between cell centres, NaN outside every tile), tiles (the TerrainTile geometry of each tile) and describe(); a field also has config and metrics (per tile, how closely it reproduced the grid when it was coded or fitted: RMSE, mean, 99th-percentile and largest error in m, slope error in degrees, seconds, bytes). Tiles are read when a query first reaches them, and the most recently used are kept. A coded field reads and decodes only the blocks of 64 x 64 cells its queries fall in, on all threads, and keeps at most cache_blocks decoded blocks for later queries, so plots scattered over a continent cost a few blocks each, never a whole tile. grid(tile) returns one tile whole from any source: the stored cells of grids, the decoded cells of a coded field, the evaluated cells of a neural field (in R, resolve.terrain_grid(), by tile name).

terrain_descriptors() 

terrain_descriptors(source, lat, lon, chunk=4096)

The four descriptors at each coordinate, read through one definition for every source: elevation, elevation_1km (the mean over the 1 km square centred on the coordinate, a 33 x 33 lattice), slope (the cell nearest the coordinate, from its four edge neighbours, as ee.Terrain.slope) and slope_1km (the inclination of the least-squares plane through the 1 km square), as (n,) float64 tensors in a TerrainDescriptors; NaN where the source holds nothing.

encode_terrain_grids() 

encode_terrain_grids(grids, config=TerrainCodecConfig(), path, tiles=[])

Codes the tiles of a TerrainGrids (all, or those named in tiles) into one coded terrain field file. TerrainCodecConfig has max_error (m, default 2: every cell is rounded to a multiple of twice this, so none moves by more) and block (cells per side of an independently coded block, default 64). Returns a dict of tile name to its metrics.

fit_terrain_tile() and assemble_terrain_field() 

fit_terrain_tile(grid, tile, config=TerrainFieldConfig(), path)
assemble_terrain_field(tiles, path)

The neural field format: one tile’s grid fitted by a multiresolution hash encoding and a small network for the detail above a coarse base, written as a tile pack; assemble_terrain_field merges tile packs into one field file. TerrainFieldConfig holds the encoding (levels, log2_table_size, features, coarsest_resolution, finest_fraction), the network (hidden_dim, n_layers), base_cells and the fit (steps, batch_size, lr, gradient_weight, seed, device). At equal size it measured 4 to 10 times further from the grid than the coded field; suites ship the coded field.

fit_terrain_correction() 

fit_terrain_correction(target, descriptor, prediction, dem, truth, dem_1km=None,
                       uncertainty_m=None, spread=None, recognised_share=None,
                       n_species=None, config=TerrainCorrectionConfig())

Fits the gated correction of one target on plots whose recorded value is truth (NaN: unrecorded, left out). descriptor is TerrainDescriptor.Elevation (an altitude target) or TerrainDescriptor.Slope. Every input is an (n,) tensor, one value per plot: the prediction, the descriptor at the coordinate and over 1 km, the recorded location uncertainty in m, the members’ standard deviation, the share of species recognised and the number of species. TerrainCorrectionConfig has scale (the target’s scale: 500 for altitude in m, 20 for slope in degrees), offset_fraction, hidden_dim, n_layers, epochs, batch_size, lr, weight_decay, dem_1km_dropout, seed and device. Returns a TerrainCorrection.

TerrainCorrection 

TerrainCorrection.load(path, device="cpu")
correction.apply(prediction, dem, dem_1km=None, uncertainty_m=None, spread=None,
                 recognised_share=None, n_species=None)
correction.save(path)

apply returns a TerrainCorrectionResult: corrected (the prediction where the correction cannot apply: no prediction or no descriptor), weights ((n, 3), the weight of the prediction, the descriptor and the 1 km descriptor; TerrainCorrection.weight_names), offset and applied. An input not given reads as the training plots’ median. The correction also has target, descriptor, config and report (the training plots and the mean absolute error of the prediction, the descriptor and the corrected value on them).

import numpy as np
import torch
import resolve_core as rc

rng = np.random.default_rng(1)
n = 4000
altitude = rng.uniform(200, 1700, n)
uncertainty = 10 ** rng.uniform(0, 3.5, n)
wrong = rng.random(n) < 0.05 + 0.15 * np.log10(uncertainty)
t = lambda x: torch.tensor(x, dtype=torch.float64)
inputs = dict(prediction=t(altitude + rng.normal(0, 30, n)),
              dem=t(altitude + rng.normal(0, 2, n) + np.where(wrong, rng.normal(0, 300, n), 0)),
              uncertainty_m=t(uncertainty))
cfg = rc.TerrainCorrectionConfig()
cfg.epochs, cfg.batch_size = 60, 256
model = rc.fit_terrain_correction("altitude", rc.TerrainDescriptor.Elevation, truth=t(altitude),
                                  config=cfg, **inputs)
print({k: round(v, 1) for k, v in model.report.items() if k.startswith("mae")})

In a suite

SuitePredictor.predict(..., terrain=...) corrects every loaded target the manifest gives a terrain correction: "field" (or True) reads the suite’s terrain field at the plots’ coordinates, {"source": "grids", "grids": dir} elevation grids, "columns" the caller’s columns named in columns["terrain"] (elevation, elevation_1km, slope, slope_1km, uncertainty; the last is read by every source). Each corrected target gets terrain, a SuiteTerrainPrediction (descriptor, source, dem, dem_1km and the result), and to_pandas() adds <target>_terrain, <target>_terrain_w_resolve, _w_dem, _w_dem_1km, <target>_dem and <target>_dem_1km.
